worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\frac{5}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}})\text{d}x & =\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-5\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
